title: Call Centres: Are You Talking To AI?

blanks.sentence: When a customer is finally connected, the worker is described as a _____ rather than a machine.
blanks.section: Part 1: Note Completion - NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS

blanks.sentence: The call-centre industry is economically _____ in countries such as India and the Philippines.
blanks.section: Part 1: Note Completion - NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS

blanks.sentence: A customer may already be aggravated and keep on _____.
At the same time, AI _____ of workers' conversations creates additional pressure.
Some workers believe that AI may replace them in the _____.
One study estimated that approximately _____ could be displaced.
The speaker believes that these gradual _____ have already begun.
AI may not completely replace human workers because it lacks _____.

multipleChoice.question: Why is the increasing use of AI in call centres a wider concern in countries such as India and the Philippines?
options: Call-centre companies there rely mainly on overseas technology.
Call-centre employment represents an important part of their economies.
Workers there have received insufficient training in artificial intelligence.
Customers there are unwilling to communicate with automated systems.

multipleChoice.question: Which situation does the call-centre worker describe as particularly difficult?
options: Recording personal information from impatient customers
Persuading customers to accept an automated solution
Correcting the AI system while continuing the conversation
Calming an angry customer while dealing with the complaint

multipleChoice.question: What additional pressure does the worker experience during a difficult call?
options: Her performance is being monitored by an AI system.
She may be replaced immediately after the call ends.
She is expected to train the robot speaking to the customer.
She is prevented from resolving the customer's concern herself.

multipleChoice.question: Why may AI monitoring make an already stressful call more difficult?
options: It requires workers to use unfamiliar technical language.
It causes customers to become more aggressive towards workers.
It evaluates workers while they are handling a demanding situation.
It makes workers responsible for repairing failures in the AI system.

multipleChoice.question: What contrast is presented regarding the role of AI in call centres?
options: AI understands customers well but performs administrative work poorly.
AI is intended to assist workers but may eventually replace them.
AI reduces the number of complaints but increases waiting times.
AI protects existing jobs but makes interactions more stressful.

multipleChoice.question: How does the worker view the displacement of call-centre employees?
options: It is a near-term process that has already begun gradually.
It is a distant possibility for which there is currently no evidence.
It is a temporary development affecting only senior employees.
It is a completed transition that has affected most workers already.

multipleChoice.question: Why does the worker believe AI cannot fully replace human call-centre staff?
options: AI cannot monitor several conversations at the same time.
AI is unable to understand the factual details of complaints.
AI cannot provide customers with solutions quickly enough.
AI lacks the empathy and compassion shown by human beings.

multipleChoice.question: Why does the speaker refer to the study predicting the displacement of 300,000 workers?
options: To explain how the call-centre industry originally developed
To prove that every call-centre employee will lose their job
To support her concern with specific numerical evidence
To compare employment levels in different countries

multipleChoice.question: What is illustrated by the comparison between speaking to a person and speaking to a robot?
options: Human workers are generally more technically accurate.
Human interaction provides a greater sense of compassion.
Customers behave more politely when AI monitors the call.
Robots can understand emotions but cannot express them.

multipleChoice.question: What is the overall implication of the discussion?
options: AI will mainly improve waiting times and make call-centre employment more secure.
The economic effects of AI will remain limited to the Philippines.
Human staff will become unnecessary once AI monitoring improves.
AI may displace workers, but its emotional limitations make full replacement uncertain.
